Lesson 3 · Business route

Make uncertainty part of the decision

Is the average online quote meaningfully different from the matched offline quote?

Fictional case. The observations are generated for teaching, not evidence about a real business. The full data-generating process is in the technical appendix.

What the data show

For 40 fictional matched products, online minus offline averages 0.79 CU. The model-based 95% interval is 0.35 to 1.22 CU.

What would you decide?

Match the same product at the same time, then judge the interval against a decision-relevant cost difference. A detectable average does not mean every product is cheaper in one channel.

Pause and explain

Does an interval above zero prove that all online quotes are higher?

Compare your reasoning

No. It concerns the population average under the model; individual paired differences vary in both directions.

What the generator knows

Reveal the known truth after making your judgment

The paired-difference generator sets the population mean to 0.45 CU. The observed average differs because this is one random sample. The other cases in this lesson have separate generators and targets.

The truth belongs to this invented model. A real organization would still need to test the assumptions and collect its own evidence.
